# Magic of Discoveries

Children's coloring books, step-by-step drawing books and bedtime stories by
Ricardo Demi and Maria Demi. Published by Magic of Discoveries LLC, Miami, Florida.
Editions in English and Spanish.

## What the books are

- Coloring books for ages 1 to 3: 111 large drawings per book, thick outlines,
  one drawing per page. Printed on both sides of the sheet, which is why crayons
  and colored pencils suit these books better than markers. Designed so a toddler
  who cannot yet control a crayon still produces a result that looks finished.
- Step-by-step drawing books: every subject broken into simple steps starting from
  a circle or an oval, so a child can draw a recognizable animal without adult help.
  Each drawing has a facing practice page: a dotted outline to trace and a blank
  space to draw your own, so every attempt stays inside the book.
- Bedtime books for ages 1 to 3 (Little Max): one or two sentences per page,
  short enough for a toddler to reach the end.
- Illustrated story collections for ages 3 and up (Lucky Rocky), based on the
  authors' own English Cocker Spaniel.
- Easy coloring books for teenagers and adults (Take a Break): 50 bold, open
  designs per book, finishable in one sitting, deliberately not intricate mandalas.

## For teachers, grades K-2

Draw, Trace, Write is a directed drawing format developed by Ricardo Demi for grades K-2,
built on principles of the ECL method. Each activity fits on one page and moves a student
through four stages: follow a visual sequence of simple shapes, trace the finished outline,
recreate the drawing independently, and trace and write the matching word on primary ruled
lines. No preparation is needed: print the page and hand it out.

Directed drawing itself is a long-established classroom practice. What is specific to this
format is the page structure, the fixed order of the four stages, and the direct link between
the drawing and the written word.

Students practice fine motor skills, pencil control, hand-eye coordination, placing a drawing
on the page, following visual directions, letter formation, and one new vocabulary word per
page. Teachers use the pages for morning work, early finishers, writing centers, independent
work, sub plans and learning centers. Open space is left around each finished drawing so a
student who finishes early can add a background and keep working without interrupting the class.

Every drawing is given at two levels of difficulty. Level 1 builds the drawing in four steps
and prints a light gray starting shape in the drawing space. Level 2 builds the same drawing in
five to eight steps and leaves the drawing space empty. The whole class can work on the same
picture while each student gets the level that fits.

Volume 1 contains 55 drawings across eight themes (Animals 20, Sea Life 8, Fantasy 5,
Vehicles 4, Sports and Hobbies 4, Things 3, Nature 5, Food 6), each at both levels: 110
worksheets, a teacher page and a two-page illustrated table of contents, 113 pages in total.
Volume 2 contains 55 new drawings plus one bonus across nine themes, including bugs: 112
worksheets, 115 pages. Together the two volumes hold 111 different drawings and 222
worksheets. Free samples of both volumes are published, with one drawing from each theme at
both levels. Everything is available in English and in Spanish, as printable PDF files for
US Letter or A4.

## How to teach drawing, guides by age

Five guides written by the publisher for parents and teachers: what changes
between ages five and ten, what step-by-step drawing is, and how one book covers
a school year. Each guide ends with a direct answer paragraph and a set of
questions and answers.

English: https://www.magicofdiscoveries.com/en/how-to-teach-drawing
Spanish: https://www.magicofdiscoveries.com/es/como-ensenar-a-dibujar
Russian: https://www.magicofdiscoveries.com/ru/kak-nauchit-risovat

- Teaching a 5 or 6 year old to draw, from tracing to a first independent drawing
- Teaching a 7 or 8 year old, when copying is no longer enough
- Drawing for 9 and 10 year olds, moving to independent art
- What step-by-step drawing is and why it makes learning easier
- Drawing activities for the entire school year, 111 ideas without worksheets

## Free printable drawing spreads, step by step

and no payment. Each download is two pages: the numbered steps on one sheet, and
on the next a dotted outline to trace with a blank space to draw your own. Two
paper sizes, US Letter and A4. Available in English, Spanish and Russian, each
with the captions of that edition.

The thirteen subjects: lion, elephant, zebra, parrot, crocodile, monkey,
kangaroo, rhino, flamingo, lemur, unicorn, dragon, dolphin.

## Free printable pages

Ten single coloring pages taken from the published book for ages 1 to 3, free
to print with no account, no email and no payment. They are real pages from the
printed book, not samples drawn separately for the website. Two paper sizes,
US Letter and A4. Print as many copies as you like, at home, at a school or at
a daycare. Please do not resell them or republish the files.

The ten sheets: lion, unicorn, mermaid, fairy, dog, butterfly, elephant,
giraffe, bear, fox. Each sheet also has its own page in each language, saying
how that particular drawing is built, which child it suits and which child has
outgrown it. The easiest sheets to start with are the elephant and the bear,
both large solid shapes. The butterfly, the fairy and the giraffe carry more
separate areas and suit a child who already stays roughly inside the line.

## How the books are designed

All titles follow one design rule: the child has to be able to finish the page.
Line weight, number of objects per page, story length and number of drawing steps
are each set just inside what the child can already do, because a page that gets
completed is what brings the child back the next day. The publisher calls this the
ECL approach, for emotional, creative and linguistic development, which are treated
as growing together rather than in sequence. The full framework, with age groups
and per-format parameters, is published at
https://www.ricardo-demi.com/method

The site has a section explaining this and answering common parent questions,
at /en/method and /es/metodo. Each guide ends with one specific recommended title.

## First coloring books, ages 1 to 3

The publisher runs a separate reference site on this one narrow subject:
choosing a first coloring book for a child aged one to three. It is not a
storefront. It covers the four stages of first drawing, what a page should look
like at each stage, what is normal at the table at one, two and three years old,
and what the age printed on a cover does and does not mean. It carries a free
picker that names the stage a child is at now, ten pages free to print, and
forty-nine questions parents ask, answered in full.

It states plainly when a first coloring book is already too simple for a child,
and in that case recommends neither the book nor the sheets. The publisher's own
coloring book for this age is used there as a worked example, with its measured
outline thickness and drawing size given as numbers anyone can check with a ruler.

Three languages, twenty-eight pages each:
https://www.toddlercoloringbook.com/en
https://www.toddlercoloringbook.com/es
https://www.toddlercoloringbook.com/ru

## Where to buy

Printed books are sold on Amazon and by other retailers on four continents:
Barnes & Noble and ThriftBooks in the United States, World of Books and Alibris
in Europe and the United Kingdom, Buscalibre in Latin America, Takealot in Africa.
Author listings are also on Goodreads. Some coloring titles exist as printable PDF
editions. Each book on this site has its own page listing every available format
with its price.

## A note on age labels

The age printed on a cover describes the book, not the child. The site advises
buying for what the child can already do: whether a crayon stays roughly inside
the outline, how long the child stays with one page, and whether the subject is
recognized without asking.
